rationale: This is a near-mechanical rediscovery of two archived signals — the second leg is identical to "Gross Margin Current Asset Discipline" and the pairing with oiadp/sale is economically the same as "Margin Turnover Improvement Confirmation" (NEG delta of WC/sales versus delta of sales/WC is a monotone reciprocal restatement), so it offers no new information channel.

Internally coherent and well-specified, but it is essentially "Cash Conversion Cycle Margin" (gen 7) with the profitability leg swapped from operating margin to persistent gross margin and the liability change deflated by cogs instead of sales — a recombination of two archived legs rather than a substantively new mechanism, and the untested cogs deflator is the only real innovation.

The negative-side working-capital-overhang channel is already covered by "Margin Turnover Deterioration Trap" (fmb −3.48, alpha −0.023) and "Profit Peak Working Capital Stretch," and the MIN construction is poorly suited to a negative expected sign because the long (low-signal) leg pools low-margin firms with disciplined-working-capital firms, making the spread economically ambiguous.

Derivative in that both legs appear separately in the archive, but pairing persistent gross margin with a genuinely cash-flow-based (oancf) working-capital-neutralized confirmation is a different information source than the balance-sheet-change discipline legs, and the sign and construction are internally consistent — though coverage will be constrained by oancf availability.

The exact ingredient pair (SG&A intensity trend × noncash current-asset intensity change) was already tested as "Cost Cut Working Capital Trap" (MUL, negative sign, ls_talpha −0.18) and "SG&A Efficiency Lean Cycle" (MIN, positive sign, ls_talpha 1.32), so this is a cosmetic re-encoding rather than a new hypothesis.

This is "Operating Margin Working Capital Turnover" (ls_alpha 0.023, t 2.65) with oiadp replaced by oibdp−xint, a trivial numerator tweak that mainly injects a leverage/interest-burden tilt rather than testing a distinct economic channel, and the hypothesis offers no reason to expect the interest deduction to add information beyond known leverage effects.
